name: Hesper Ndiaye
equipment: Cognition diagnostic slate with a hard-jack lead
Portable substrate analyser (the size of a lunchbox, very expensive, borrowed)
A printed copy of her own paper, 'Continuity and Custody: Uploaded Minds Under the Statutes', heavily annotated in someone else's hand
Cooled suit liner for working in hot machine spaces
features: Augmented: Optic Suite (Enhanced: darkvision 60 ft; gold-flecked irises that adjust visibly)
Analyze (bonus action: study a creature, device or situation; the next attack roll or check an ally makes against it before her next turn has advantage; 3 uses per short rest)
Polymath (proficient in Science, Computers and Mechanics; adds +1, half proficiency, to any Intelligence check she is not proficient in)
Eureka (once per long rest, after a failed Intelligence check, reroll it with a +5 bonus)
Researcher (Academic feature: she can get access to university archives and specialist libraries, and academics will usually answer her questions)

personality.traits: I explain things nobody asked about, with diagrams if I can find a surface. I take notes during firefights.
personality.ideals: A mind is a mind, whatever it's running on. I used to think that was a philosophical position. Now I think it's the only one.
personality.bonds: My paper was cited in the legal judgement that made uploaded minds property under the Continuity Statutes. I argued the opposite. The court quoted the half that suited it. I have been trying to get it unquoted for nine years.
personality.flaws: I trust evidence over people, and I'm usually right to. The one time I'm wrong will be the time it matters.

appearance: A compact, intense woman of forty-four, dark-skinned, with close natural hair streaked grey at one temple and gold-flecked eyes, the visible sign of her optic augmentation, which adjust like a camera aperture when she's thinking. She wears a field jacket over academic clothes and carries far too many slates.
backstory: Dr. Hesper Ndiaye is the inner system's leading authority on the legal and physical continuity of uploaded minds, which in practice means corporations pay her to say whether a substrate holds a person or only a model of one. Mabb hired her to authenticate Lot Zero and make sure the 'lattice' survives transport. Hesper read the reserve price, the power draw and the name 'Vell Engine', and remembered that Isaura Vell was the dive engineer who died aboard the Aubade nine years ago, the same year a Statute case was decided using Hesper's own paper. She hasn't told the crew what she suspects. She isn't sure yet, and she needs to be sure, because if she's right she wrote part of the reason this woman has been in a box for nine years.
